title: Dobby Owner Recovery Response v2
description: Wire shape of the vendor-signed owner recovery response the host imports (controlling authority: ADR-0058 § Owner recovery v2; selector namespaces: ADR-0062 § 1; observable flow: docs/specs/session-lifecycle.md). ADR-0039 is the superseded predecessor whose 5-source hardware-threshold binding this shape replaces; it is history and is not citable as current authority. Schema validity proves shape only, and it is not even the whole of artifact verification. Artifact verification adds a P1363 signature from a trusted vendor recovery key, purpose binding, keyId agreement between payload and signature, and a bounded validity window. Authorization to mutate an owner credential requires more than that: the host import flow must also match this response against the pending RecoveryRequests ledger row (binding fields, SHA-256 nonce-hash equality, globally unique responseId, re-hashed payload integrity), and it must re-run that match inside the mutation transaction and burn the request with a conditional single-row update. No v1 response is readable and no owner credential is mutated before all of those pass.

keyId.$comment: Cross-field obligation JSON Schema cannot express: this keyId MUST equal payload.keyId, and a verifier MUST reject a mismatch before trusting the payload. Selecting the verification key from one member while taking authority from the other would accept a substituted key identity (ADR-0062 keyId selector).

ADR-0062 § 1 canonical vendor selector <purpose-short>-<prod|test>-<YYYY-MM>. purpose-short is bijective with the signing purpose, so a recovery response may only name a key from the recovery ring; a plugin-package or license selector here is a shape violation rejected before signature verification (key-purpose confusion, ADR-0059). Format conformance is not trust: the host still requires an exact match in its recovery ring.

utc.$comment: Field ranges are bounded, not merely digit-counted: a two-digit-per-component pattern accepts 2026-99-99T99:99:99Z, which reaches the typed parser as an out-of-range instant and turns a shape error into a parse/arithmetic failure path (range overflow). Residual calendar validity the pattern cannot express -- 2026-02-30, non-leap 02-29 -- stays with the typed parser; leap-second :60 is deliberately outside the accepted set.
